_purpose: Questions registered BEFORE the data exists. Pre-registration is the whole point: deciding what counts as an answer after seeing results is how noise becomes a conclusion.
_method: Two-sample comparison of mean R, power 0.8 at alpha 0.05, so n per group is about 16/d^2. Effect sizes are the smallest difference worth acting on, not the one hoped for.

operational.question: Does a full session complete without the alarm chain dying?
Does at least one entry clear every gate in a live session?
Do submitted orders reconcile to actual fills and positions?
Are gate rejections for substantive reasons rather than data defects?
Does the LLM budget last a full session at the configured cadence?
Does every trade produce an entry thesis and an exit attribution?
After the record becomes non-empty, do entry rates fall or refusals cluster after losing streaks?

statistical.question: Do guidance-raise catalysts produce a higher mean R than earnings beats?
statistical.falsified_if: earnings mean R is equal or higher once both groups reach the sample

statistical.question: Do discretionary exits produce a higher mean R than trades that ran to a level?
statistical.falsified_if: discretionary mean R is lower, which would argue for removing the LLM sell path

statistical.question: Do trades entered above 0.80 model confidence produce a higher mean R than those below 0.70?
statistical.falsified_if: no separation, which would mean confidence should stop scaling position size

statistical.question: Do entries above 75% of the 52-week high produce a higher mean R than those between 70 and 75%?
statistical.falsified_if: no separation, which would argue for lowering the gate and taking more trades

statistical.question: Do insider open-market purchase clusters produce a higher mean R than earnings beats?
statistical.falsified_if: insider clusters do not beat earnings beats, which would argue for dropping the source rather than keeping a sixth input that adds no edge
statistical.registered: 2026-09-12, before the source produced a single trade

statistical.question: Do gap-captured exits produce a higher mean R than the same positions held to a level would have?
statistical.falsified_if: gap capture underperforms, which would mean the gap continues more often than it fades and the rule is cutting winners
statistical.note: Tension with post-earnings drift: the literature says the move continues, while a live example gave the whole gap back overnight. Set at 1.5R to match the trail arm rather than to fit that one trade; 1.0R would have caught it but cuts more winners.
statistical.registered: 2026-09-12, before the rule has fired once

statistical.question: Do entries taken with RSI(14) in 40-52 realise a lower mean R than entries outside that band?
statistical.falsified_if: in-band mean R is equal or higher once both groups reach the sample, or the sign flips between two consecutive reviews
statistical.mechanism: Sizing sets the target at target_r_multiple x stop. That arithmetic only pays if forward travel is asymmetric. Measured over 10 days on 12,620 daily bars, MFE/MAE inside the band is 1.18 against 1.35 outside it, conditional on the 52w and range-position gates already applied. Near-equal excursion means a 2R target is a structure the price path does not honour. This is a claim about risk geometry, not direction: no prediction is made about which way price goes.
statistical.evidence_at_registration: 10 large caps, Sep 2021-Sep 2026. Worse in-band in 10 of 10 symbols and 5 of 6 years; 2023 (the AI melt-up) is the exception. Unconditional gap 0.21, falling to 0.167 once the live gates are applied, so roughly a fifth of the effect is already captured by existing gates.
statistical.known_weaknesses: The 40-52 boundary was fitted on the same sample it was tested on, which is why this is registered rather than enforced. MFE/MAE over a fixed 10-day window with no stop is not realised P&L, and the sample drifts upward, so only the difference between buckets is load-bearing. All ten names are survivors.
statistical.expected_timeline: About 27% of gate-passing candidates fall in the band, so at 3 trades/week the in-band group gains roughly 0.8 trades/week and 64 trades takes over a year. Slow by construction; recorded now so the question is answerable later rather than reconstructed after the fact.
statistical.decision_if_supported: Do not add a veto. Lower target_r_multiple for in-band entries so the target sits inside the excursion the band actually delivers. A veto removes one candidate in four from a system whose binding problem is too few trades, not too many.
